Presentation
Page Presentation
The navigation page Presentation contains on the one hand a Presentation with the most important information for the offer at the customer and the documentation of system design. On the other hand the page contains exportable Simulation Results.
To adapt the presentation, the document template and the language of the presentation can be set via Options. The Preview area provides options for configuring the display behavior and printing the presentation. In the area Export, the presentation can be exported as *.pdf and as *.docx file.
Options
Document template:
Currently available document templates are Customer presentation - Compact, Customer presentation and Documentation. In the Project Options you can edit the existing templates or create new ones. For each document template you can define which layout should be used and (with the exception of the layout “Customer presentation - Compact”) which chapters should be part of the presentation.
Language in document:
The language of the presentation can be selected here. Currently 27 languages are available.

Via the buttons and the presentation can be exported as *.pdf and as *.docx file. If the option Open file after export is activated, the exported file is opened directly after the export. The program assigned to the respective file extension by the Windows operating system is used for this purpose.
Project options Presentation
Here you can make further settings regarding the presentation. These settings are project-related, i.e. they apply to the current project.
Configuration Presentation
Document template
Use the drop-down menu to select a document template. For each selected document template, you can specify the Layout and Contents of the presentation. The button bar next to the drop-down menu provides further configuration options. You can reset the selected document template, save changes, rename, delete, export, create your own document templates, or import a template.
Button bar next to the drop-down menu:
Basic functions: 
Restore template: If the settings for the layout or content of the presentation of the current project differ from the document template, you can restore the template, i.e. apply the template settings to the current project.
Save template: You can choose whether the selected document template should be overwritten with the settings of the current project or whether you want to save the settings of the current project as a new template.
Other functions: 
Rename template
Delete template
Import template from file
Export template: You can choose whether to export the selected document template (without taking into account any differences between the template and the settings of the current project), or to export the settings of the current project
Indication of deviations of the settings of the current project from the document template: If the settings for the layout or content of the current project differ from the document template, this is indicated by “●” in front of the respective document template. In addition, the deviation of the template or the deviating nodes in the tree view for the content is also marked accordingly. 
Layout
Depending on the selected layout, the structure of the presentation varies.
Customer presentation - Compact: Short presentation in which the most relevant information is presented in a visually appealing way 
Please note: With this layout, the content of the presentation cannot be freely defined.
Customer presentation: Structure and content of the title page and headers are customer-oriented, i.e. they contain the information relevant to your customers, e.g.: 
The title page has a letterhead, the recipient field contains the name and address of the customer data provided in the project
In addition, the front page contains detailed contact information about the person or company sending the message
The content of the presentation can be freely defined (see below)
Documentation: Title page and headers contain the information relevant for your documentation of the plant design, e.g: 
The title page has no letterhead and is structured fundamentally different from the title page of the customer presentation
The title page contains all customer and project data specified in the project.
The content of the presentation can be freely defined (see below)
Contents
For each document template (except when the “Customer Presentation - Compact” layout is chosen), you can define which chapters are to be part of the presentation. To do this, activate or deactivate the contents in the tree view for the respective document template.
When activating/deactivating the contents, the respective sub nodes are activated/deactivated by holding down the CTRL key. 
Some content is gray and in brackets although it is enabled. This is the case if the content does not match the opened project (e.g. data sheet electric vehicle, if the project does not contain an electric vehicle). By activating the option Hide contents not matching the project, these contents will be hidden. 
Further Options
Language in document:
The language of the presentation can be selected here. Currently 27 languages are available.
If -- Like program language -- is selected, the current PV*SOL® program language is used.
With the option Show preview automatically you can define whether the presentation is created and displayed automatically if required. This is the case, for example, if you switch from another page to the Presentation page, but also if another language or document template is selected. If this option is deactivated, the creation and display of the presentation on the Presentation page must be started manually.
With the option Open file after export you can determine whether an exported presentation (*.pdf or *.docx file) is opened directly after the export. The program assigned to the respective file extension by the Windows operating system is used for this purpose.
With the option Screenshots in landscape format it can be determined whether screenshots from the 3D design are inserted into the presentation in landscape format or in portrait format.

### Project options Presentation

Here you can make further settings regarding the presentation. These settings are project-related, i.e. they apply to the current project.

[![](/pvsol/images/navigationsseiten/praesentation/page_optionenPraesentation.en.png)](https://help.valentin-software.com/pvsol/images/navigationsseiten/praesentation/page_optionenPraesentation.en.png)

#### Configuration Presentation

#### Document template

Use the drop-down menu to select a document template. For each selected document template, you can specify the [Layout](https://help.valentin-software.com/pvsol/en/pages/presentation/#layout) and [Contents](https://help.valentin-software.com/pvsol/en/pages/presentation/#contents) of the presentation. The button bar next to the drop-down menu provides further configuration options. You can reset the selected document template, save changes, rename, delete, export, create your own document templates, or import a template.

Button bar next to the drop-down menu:

*   Basic functions:
    *   ![](/pvsol/images/buttons/btn_undo.png) Restore template: If the settings for the layout or content of the presentation of the current project differ from the document template, you can restore the template, i.e. apply the template settings to the current project.
    *   ![](/pvsol/images/buttons/btn_speichern_dropdown.png) Save template: You can choose whether the selected document template should be overwritten with the settings of the current project or whether you want to save the settings of the current project as a new template.
*   Other functions:
    *   ![](/pvsol/images/buttons/btn_bearbeiten.png) Rename template
    *   ![](/pvsol/images/icons/icon_zeileEntfernen.png) Delete template
    *   ![](/pvsol/images/icons/icon_import.png) Import template from file
    *   ![](/pvsol/images/icons/icon_export.png) Export template: You can choose whether to export the selected document template (without taking into account any differences between the template and the settings of the current project), or to export the settings of the current project

**Indication of deviations of the settings of the current project from the document template:** If the settings for the layout or content of the current project differ from the document template, this is indicated by “●” in front of the respective document template. In addition, the deviation of the template or the deviating nodes in the tree view for the content is also marked accordingly.

#### Layout

Depending on the selected layout, the structure of the presentation varies.

*   Customer presentation - Compact: Short presentation in which the most relevant information is presented in a visually appealing way
    *   _Please note:_ With this layout, the content of the presentation cannot be freely defined.
*   Customer presentation: Structure and content of the title page and headers are customer-oriented, i.e. they contain the information relevant to your customers, e.g.:
    *   The title page has a letterhead, the recipient field contains the name and address of the customer data provided in the project
    *   In addition, the front page contains detailed contact information about the person or company sending the message
    *   The content of the presentation can be freely defined (see [below](https://help.valentin-software.com/pvsol/en/pages/presentation/#contents))
*   Documentation: Title page and headers contain the information relevant for your documentation of the plant design, e.g:
    *   The title page has no letterhead and is structured fundamentally different from the title page of the customer presentation
    *   The title page contains all customer and project data specified in the project.
    *   The content of the presentation can be freely defined (see [below](https://help.valentin-software.com/pvsol/en/pages/presentation/#contents))

#### Contents

For each document template (except when the “Customer Presentation - Compact” layout is chosen), you can define which chapters are to be part of the presentation. To do this, activate or deactivate the contents in the tree view for the respective document template.

When activating/deactivating the contents, the respective sub nodes are activated/deactivated by holding down the `CTRL` key.

Some content is gray and in brackets although it is enabled. This is the case if the content does not match the opened project (e.g. data sheet electric vehicle, if the project does not contain an electric vehicle). By activating the option ![](/pvsol/images/check-checked.png) Hide contents not matching the project, these contents will be hidden.

#### Further Options

Language in document:  
The language of the presentation can be selected here. Currently 27 languages are available.  
If \-- Like program language -- is selected, the current PV\*SOL® program language is used.

With the option ![](/pvsol/images/check-checked.png) Show preview automatically you can define whether the presentation is created and displayed automatically if required. This is the case, for example, if you switch from another page to the _Presentation_ page, but also if another language or document template is selected. If this option is deactivated, the creation and display of the presentation on the _Presentation_ page must be started manually.

With the option ![](/pvsol/images/check-checked.png) Open file after export you can determine whether an exported presentation (`*.pdf` or `*.docx` file) is opened directly after the export. The program assigned to the respective file extension by the Windows operating system is used for this purpose.

With the option ![](/pvsol/images/check-checked.png) Screenshots in landscape format it can be determined whether screenshots from the 3D design are inserted into the presentation in landscape format or in portrait format.

Plans and Parts list
Overview of the page Plans and Parts list
All technical drawings and plans are displayed on the plans page. PV*SOL® can create the following plans:
Schematic circuit diagram
Dimension plan (only for 3D design )
String diagram (only for 3D design)
Parts list
The plans can be adapted via the menu item Options and exported to different formats via Export. Different export formats are available for the export depending on the plan.
Plan-dependent overview of export formats
Plan Export formats 
Schematic circuit diagram	PDF, PNG, SVG	
		
Dimensioning plan	PDF, PNG, DXF	
String diagram	PDF, PNG, DXF	
Parts list	CSV	
Schematic circuit diagram
Detail view circuit diagram
The circuit diagram is a representation of your PV system with standardized circuit symbols. The following options can be set in the menu item Options:
Legend 
Display of the circuit symbols used and more detailed product information. The legend can be anchored at different positions in the plan.
Drawing frame 
A drawing frame according to EN ISO 5457 is spanned around the circuit diagram and a title block according to EN ISO 7200 is created. The title block is filled with the project data.
Plan Properties 
In the Plan Properties dialog the page format and the alignment of the schematic can be adjusted. In addition, the scaling and color of the schematic can be changed. 
Scaling options 
Adapt to page format 
The display size of the schematic is adapted to the available drawing area.
None 
The display size of the schematic remains unchanged. If the size of the circuit diagram exceeds the drawing area, the diagram is reduced in size.
Colour options 
Circuit diagram 
You can choose Background coloured and Cables coloured. Multiple selection is also possible.
Legend 
Here you can change the color of the legend.
Dialogue plan properties
All settings made are automatically saved and serve as templates for all further projects or circuit diagrams.
Dimension plan
Detail view dimensioning plan
When closing the 3D visualization, dimension plans are automatically generated for all occupancy areas on which PV modules are located. Here it is sufficient if an allocation surface was interconnected. The floor plans of the occupancy objects and lock objects are displayed in black and the PV modules in blue on the dimension plan. For mounted systems, the module rows are also displayed. The following dimensions are also displayed in the plan:
Roof-parallel system:
Dimensions of roof edges
Distance of the first module formation to the left and lower roof edge
The dimensions (width x length) of a module
The horizontal and vertical module spacings
Mounted system:
Row spacing
Alignment to the occupancy area using the example of a module row
The following options can be set in the menu item Options:
Dimensions 
Showing and hiding dimensions
Black/White 
Black and white display of the dimensioning plan
String diagram
Detail view string diagram
When the 3D visualization is closed, string plans are automatically generated for all occupancy areas on which connected PV modules are located. The floor plans of the occupancy objects and lock objects are displayed in black and the PV modules in blue on the string diagram. For mounted systems, the module rows are also displayed.
The following options can be set in the menu item Options:
Caption 
Show and hide module labels
Black/White 
Black and white display of the string plan
Parts list
A parts list is automatically generated from the individual products used in project planning. An article number can be stored for each of these products.
Detail view parts list
The article numbers are automatically saved and are available when the same product is used again without having to enter them again. If a product is not to be part of the exported parts list, visibility can be deactivated. The column “Fix” determines whether an article should appear in the parts lists of your projects in general. The parts list can be supplemented with articles that are not automatically inserted by PV*SOL®. The finished parts list can be exported to a comma-separated file (CSV) for further use.

[![](/pvsol/images/navigationsseiten/plaene/page_plaene.en.png)](https://help.valentin-software.com/pvsol/images/navigationsseiten/plaene/page_plaene.en.png)

#### Overview of the page Plans and Parts list

All technical drawings and plans are displayed on the ![](/pvsol/images/navigationsseiten/icon_plaene.png) _plans_ page. PV\*SOL® can create the following plans:

*   [Schematic circuit diagram](https://help.valentin-software.com/pvsol/en/pages/plans-and-parts-list/#schematic-circuit-diagram)
*   [Dimension plan](https://help.valentin-software.com/pvsol/en/pages/plans-and-parts-list/#dimension-plan) (only for ![](/pvsol/images/navigationsseiten/icon_3d-planung.z.png)[3D design](https://help.valentin-software.com/pvsol/en/pages/3d-design/) )
*   [String diagram](https://help.valentin-software.com/pvsol/en/pages/plans-and-parts-list/#schematic-circuit-diagram) (only for ![](/pvsol/images/navigationsseiten/icon_3d-planung.z.png)[3D design](https://help.valentin-software.com/pvsol/en/pages/3d-design/))
*   [Parts list](https://help.valentin-software.com/pvsol/en/pages/plans-and-parts-list/#parts-list)

The plans can be adapted via the menu item Options and exported to different formats via Export. Different export formats are available for the export depending on the plan.

_Plan-dependent overview of export formats_

| Plan | Export formats |
| --- | --- |
| Schematic circuit diagram | PDF, PNG, SVG |
|     |     |
| Dimensioning plan | PDF, PNG, DXF |
| String diagram | PDF, PNG, DXF |
| Parts list | CSV |

### Schematic circuit diagram

[![](/pvsol/images/navigationsseiten/plaene/page_schaltplan.en.png)](https://help.valentin-software.com/pvsol/images/navigationsseiten/plaene/page_schaltplan.en.png)

#### Detail view circuit diagram

The circuit diagram is a representation of your PV system with standardized circuit symbols. The following options can be set in the menu item Options:

*   **Legend**  
    Display of the circuit symbols used and more detailed product information. The legend can be anchored at different positions in the plan.
*   **Drawing frame**  
    A drawing frame according to EN ISO 5457 is spanned around the circuit diagram and a title block according to EN ISO 7200 is created. The title block is filled with the project data.
*   **Plan Properties**  
    In the Plan Properties dialog the page format and the alignment of the schematic can be adjusted. In addition, the scaling and color of the schematic can be changed.
    *   **Scaling options**  
        *   _Adapt to page format_  
            The display size of the schematic is adapted to the available drawing area.
        *   _None_  
            The display size of the schematic remains unchanged. If the size of the circuit diagram exceeds the drawing area, the diagram is reduced in size.
    *   **Colour options**  
        *   Circuit diagram  
            You can choose ![](/pvsol/images/check-unchecked.png) Background coloured and ![](/pvsol/images/check-unchecked.png) Cables coloured. Multiple selection is also possible.
        *   Legend  
            Here you can change the color of the legend.

[![](/pvsol/images/navigationsseiten/plaene/page_planEigenschaften.en.png)](https://help.valentin-software.com/pvsol/images/navigationsseiten/plaene/page_planEigenschaften.en.png)

#### Dialogue plan properties

All settings made are automatically saved and serve as templates for all further projects or circuit diagrams.

### Dimension plan

[![](/pvsol/images/navigationsseiten/plaene/page_bemassungsplan.en.png)](https://help.valentin-software.com/pvsol/images/navigationsseiten/plaene/page_bemassungsplan.en.png)

#### Detail view dimensioning plan

When closing the 3D visualization, dimension plans are automatically generated for all occupancy areas on which PV modules are located. Here it is sufficient if an allocation surface was interconnected. The floor plans of the occupancy objects and lock objects are displayed in black and the PV modules in blue on the dimension plan. For mounted systems, the module rows are also displayed. The following dimensions are also displayed in the plan:

Roof-parallel system:

*   Dimensions of roof edges
*   Distance of the first module formation to the left and lower roof edge
*   The dimensions (width x length) of a module
*   The horizontal and vertical module spacings

Mounted system:

*   Row spacing
*   Alignment to the occupancy area using the example of a module row

The following options can be set in the menu item Options:

*   **Dimensions**  
    Showing and hiding dimensions
*   **Black/White**  
    Black and white display of the dimensioning plan

### String diagram

[![](/pvsol/images/navigationsseiten/plaene/page_strangplan.en.png)](https://help.valentin-software.com/pvsol/images/navigationsseiten/plaene/page_strangplan.en.png)

#### Detail view string diagram

When the 3D visualization is closed, string plans are automatically generated for all occupancy areas on which connected PV modules are located. The floor plans of the occupancy objects and lock objects are displayed in black and the PV modules in blue on the string diagram. For mounted systems, the module rows are also displayed.

The following options can be set in the menu item Options:

*   **Caption**  
    Show and hide module labels
*   **Black/White**  
    Black and white display of the string plan

### Parts list

A parts list is automatically generated from the individual products used in project planning. An article number can be stored for each of these products.

[![](/pvsol/images/navigationsseiten/plaene/page_stueckliste.en.png)](https://help.valentin-software.com/pvsol/images/navigationsseiten/plaene/page_stueckliste.en.png)

#### Detail view parts list

The article numbers are automatically saved and are available when the same product is used again without having to enter them again. If a product is not to be part of the exported parts list, visibility can be deactivated. The column “Fix” ![](/pvsol/images/navigationsseiten/plaene/fixieren.png) determines whether an article should appear in the parts lists of your projects in general. The parts list can be supplemented with articles that are not automatically inserted by PV\*SOL®. The finished parts list can be exported to a comma-separated file (CSV) for further use.

# Pro: Document Management

With Easy PV Pro's document management options, all project files – surveys, proposals, reports, customer documents – can be stored in one place, with no need for a separate QMS system. This allows you to keep track of everything you need for a project in one place. Documents uploaded here can also be attached to any [emails sent within the Easy PV](https://help.easy-pv.co.uk/books/reports-documents-and-emails/page/pro-sending-emails-from-easy-pv "Pro: Emailing").

* * *

The document management section can be found at the bottom left of the project overview.

**[![image.png](https://help.easy-pv.co.uk/uploads/images/gallery/2025-11/scaled-1680-/w2JGBCgnPu6z24J8-image.png)](https://help.easy-pv.co.uk/uploads/images/gallery/2025-11/w2JGBCgnPu6z24J8-image.png)**

## **Uploading files to the document manager**

Files can be saved directly from a project or uploaded from your device. These can also be sent in emails through Easy PV. If you have team files you'd like accessible on all projects when sending emails, you can upload these to your team uploads. 

### Saving an Easy PV report to the document manager

When previewing any report in Easy PV, on the **right-hand** sidebar there will be an orange **`Save`** button at the bottom. Click this to save the file to the document manager.

[![image.png](https://help.easy-pv.co.uk/uploads/images/gallery/2025-11/scaled-1680-/OFxArVahIqONDbiM-image.png)](https://help.easy-pv.co.uk/uploads/images/gallery/2025-11/OFxArVahIqONDbiM-image.png)

**Note**: If you make changes to a document, you will need to re-save it for the updates to appear in the document manager. When re-saving a document, the **`Save`** button will be grey and saving will override previously saved version. 

### Upload a document from your device

To upload a document from your device, click `**Upload**` . Then use the `**Upload File**` button to find the document you wish to upload. 

[![image.png](https://help.easy-pv.co.uk/uploads/images/gallery/2025-11/scaled-1680-/knSK0fQwA4cIcavX-image.png)](https://help.easy-pv.co.uk/uploads/images/gallery/2025-11/knSK0fQwA4cIcavX-image.png)

* * *

## Options on saved files

[![image.png](https://help.easy-pv.co.uk/uploads/images/gallery/2025-11/scaled-1680-/FhQcfz1hWcLSZmjx-image.png)](https://help.easy-pv.co.uk/uploads/images/gallery/2025-11/FhQcfz1hWcLSZmjx-image.png)

To edit the details on any saved files, click the **⋯ three dots**. You will then see the following options: 

*    **[![Edit.jpg](https://help.easy-pv.co.uk/uploads/images/gallery/2025-11/scaled-1680-/6M6gz1NJneGPPmZb-edit.jpg)](https://help.easy-pv.co.uk/uploads/images/gallery/2025-11/6M6gz1NJneGPPmZb-edit.jpg) Rename**Change the name of the file. Note that the file name will display if it's sent in any emails in Easy PV
*   **[![Switch.jpg](https://help.easy-pv.co.uk/uploads/images/gallery/2025-11/scaled-1680-/Tq74w8GDZVKo8Md8-switch.jpg)](https://help.easy-pv.co.uk/uploads/images/gallery/2025-11/Tq74w8GDZVKo8Md8-switch.jpg)Reassign

### Have you heard of K2 Base?

Our innovative planning tool, K2 Base, enables fast, secure and accurate planning of PV projects. In just five steps, you can determine the optimal design of your K2 mounting system and the configuration of your PV project. And it’s all free of charge!

*   Intuitive editor for drawing roofs and module fields
*   Automatic determination of loads and obstacle detection
*   Automatic calculation and display of roof fasteners and ballasting
*   Complete results report with structural analysis and installation plans
*   Data can be transferred directly to various planning tools and directly to the dealer’s shopping basket

## Summary:

Learn how to create and customize a **Swipe proposal** in OpenSolar. Swipe proposals provide an interactive, chapter-based experience designed for residential sales, allowing customers to move through system details, savings, pricing, and next steps on any device. This guide covers creating a reusable Swipe template, customizing pages and content, applying it to a project, and sharing the finished proposal with your customer.

## Table of contents

*   Swipe vs Scroll proposals
*   Before you start
*   Create a Swipe proposal template
*   Preview and edit your Swipe template
*   Customize your Swipe template
*   Open a Swipe proposal on a project
*   Customize the proposal for a specific project
*   Send and share the proposal
*   Limits and troubleshooting
*   Related articles

## Swipe vs Scroll proposals

OpenSolar offers two proposal experiences: **Swipe** and **Scroll**.

|     | Swipe | Scroll |
| --- | --- | --- |
| **Style** | Interactive, chapter-based proposal | Long-form, scrolling document |
| **Best for** | Visual residential sales presentations | Detailed proposals, quotations, and PDFs |
| **Template** | **Swipe** | **Scroll**, tagged **Classic** |
| **Commercial projects** | Not available | Available |

You can create and use both template types within your organization and choose the experience that best fits each project.

This article focuses specifically on **Swipe proposals**, previously known as **Sales Machine**.

For a more detailed overview of all Swipe functionality, see the [Swipe Proposal User Guide](https://support.opensolar.com/hc/en-us/articles/13782333913231-Swipe-Proposal-User-Guide).

## Before you start

Before creating a Swipe proposal, make sure your organization and project are ready.

### Organization requirements

*   **Swipe must be available for your organization.** If you do not see a **Swipe** template card, contact OpenSolar Support.
*   You need permission to manage **Proposal Templates**.
*   Add your company logo and highlight color under **Control > Company > Business Info** so your branding appears correctly throughout the proposal.

For more information, see [How to Add or Update Business Information](https://support.opensolar.com/hc/en-us/articles/4408425960217).

### Project requirements

Before opening Swipe on a project:

1.  Make sure the project is **residential**. Swipe is not available for commercial projects.
2.  Complete a valid **Design** with at least one system.
3.  Add **Payment Options** if you want to display savings, financial information, or checkout.
4.  Make sure **six or fewer systems** are selected for the proposal, including electrification systems. If more are selected, reduce them from the **Payments** tab.
5.  Add a customer **Contact** if you plan to email the proposal through OpenSolar.

**Note:** Swipe template previews use standard Design projects rather than Quick Quote projects.

## Create a Swipe proposal template

Swipe templates are created at the organization level, allowing you to configure them once and reuse them across multiple projects.

To create a Swipe template:

1.  Open **Control** from the top-left corner.
2.  Go to **Purchase Experience > Proposal Template**.
3.  Click **\+ Proposal Template**.
4.  Under **Sales Machine Proposal Templates**, select **Swipe**.
5.  Optional: Select **Demo** on the Swipe card to preview a sample proposal before creating your own.
6.  Enter a **Title** for the template, such as _Residential Swipe_.
7.  Add an optional **Description**, **Template Image**, or archive status.
8.  Save the template.
9.  Select **Full Screen** to begin editing the proposal using live project data.

The **Template Image** appears as the thumbnail your team sees when choosing a proposal template from a project.

Unlike Scroll templates, Swipe templates do not use the same **Is Default** setting. Your team selects the Swipe template from the template library on the project's **Proposal** tab.

## Preview and edit your Swipe template

The template editor lets you preview the customer experience while making changes.

### Select a preview project

Choose a residential project with completed systems and payment options so the preview can display realistic project information.

For the best results, select a project that represents a typical customer sale.

If you see the message:

**This project doesn't contain enough information to generate a Sales Machine Swipe proposal**

select another project with a valid design and payment options.

### Open Full Screen

Select **Full Screen** to open the full Swipe editor.

The editor includes:

*   A live proposal preview
*   Page controls
*   Editing tools
*   Proposal settings
*   Device previews

Use the device selector to preview the proposal on **desktop, tablet, and mobile**.

Where available, select **View as customer** to experience the proposal as your customer will see it.

When you're finished editing, select **Save** from the full-screen toolbar.

### How customers navigate Swipe

Swipe proposals are organized into chapters.

Common chapters include:

*   **Home** — Cover and introduction
*   **Energy** — Energy usage and proposed system
*   **Savings** — Bill savings and financial information
*   **Go** — Quotation, next steps, and checkout

On **mobile and tablet**, customers swipe between pages.

On **desktop**, customers can move through the proposal using the on-screen arrows or keyboard arrow keys.

## Customize your Swipe template

Swipe gives you control over the proposal structure, page content, branding, financial displays, and checkout experience.

Some settings are available from the main **Proposal Template** page, while page-level design and content changes are made in the **Full Screen** editor.

### Featured Figures

Choose the headline metrics you want to highlight throughout the proposal, such as:

*   System size
*   First-year savings
*   Payback period
*   Other financial or system metrics

Select figures that best support your sales process and are most useful to your customers.

### Disclaimers

Add or customize disclaimers for different sections of the proposal, including:

*   Hardware
*   System performance
*   Bill savings
*   Quotation
*   Cash payment options
*   Loans
*   PPAs
*   Leases

### Advanced Settings

Use **Advanced Settings** to control additional proposal behavior.

#### Proposal checkout

Choose whether customers can accept the proposal online.

You can:

*   Enable checkout
*   Disable checkout
*   Automatically disable checkout when the proposal expires
*   Add a custom message when checkout is unavailable

#### Bill savings chart

Choose whether to hide the export credit breakdown from the cumulative bill savings chart.

#### Net financial impact chart

Lock the minimum and maximum chart axes so different payment options use the same scale, making comparisons easier for customers.

### Template Image

Add an image to represent the template within the project template library.

This can help your team quickly identify the correct proposal when multiple Swipe templates are available.

## Customize pages in Full Screen

Open **Full Screen** from the organization template or from a project's proposal.

The left sidebar includes three main areas:

*   **Pages**
*   **Edit**
*   **Settings**

### Pages

Use **Pages** to control the structure of the proposal.

Depending on the page type, you can:

*   Add pages
*   Hide pages
*   Rename pages
*   Reorder pages
*   Delete supported pages

Select **Page** to open the available **Page Templates**.

Available templates can include:

#### Brand pages

*   Cover Page Style 1
*   Cover Page Style 2
*   Cover Page Style 3
*   About Us
*   Customer Testimonials
*   Our Solar Services
*   Video Page

![](/hc/article_attachments/16277040786703)

#### Graph pages

*   System Performance
*   How Your System Works
*   Bill Savings
*   Net Financial Impact

#### Layout pages

Where available:

*   Blank Page
*   1 Column
*   2 Column
*   3 Column

Swipe pages use predefined, structured layouts rather than free-form drag-and-drop placement.

For more information, see [Pages and Edit in the Swipe Proposal Editor](https://support.opensolar.com/hc/en-us/articles/13440011613071).

![](/hc/article_attachments/16277040786063)

### Edit

Select a page and open **Edit** to change supported content.

Depending on the page, you may be able to update:

*   Text
*   Images
*   Typography
*   Other page-specific content

Select an editable area directly from the preview to open its available settings.

Changes appear in the proposal preview as you make them.

For more information, see [Editing in the Sales Machine Proposal](https://support.opensolar.com/hc/en-us/articles/13440054388239).

### Settings

Use **Settings** to manage proposal-level options such as:

*   **Language**
*   **Valid Until** date
*   **Contract Template**

Save your changes from the full-screen toolbar before leaving the editor.

## Open a Swipe proposal on a project

Once your template is ready:

1.  Open a residential project.
2.  Make sure the Design and relevant Payment Options are complete.
3.  Go to the **Proposal** tab.
4.  The template library will open with the message **Choose a template to create a proposal for your customer**.
5.  Select the **Swipe** template you want to use.
6.  OpenSolar will generate the proposal using the project's design, payment options, and your Swipe template.

On a new project, the template library may open automatically the first time you visit the Proposal tab.

If both Swipe and Scroll templates are available, you can choose which experience you want to use for that customer.

## Customize the proposal for a specific project

You can make project-level changes without changing the organization template.

Open the project's proposal and select **Full Screen**.

From here, you can update:

*   Pages
*   Page content
*   Language
*   Validity date
*   Contract template
*   Other supported proposal settings

These changes apply to that project only.

### If the organization template is updated

If the original Swipe template is changed after a project proposal has already been customized, the template card may display **Updated**.

When you select the updated version, OpenSolar may warn that applying it will overwrite the project's current proposal.

Choose:

*   **Override** — Apply the latest organization template and overwrite the project's customized version.
*   **Cancel** — Keep the project's existing customized proposal.

Use **Override** carefully if the project contains customer-specific page or content changes.

## Send and share the proposal

Once the proposal is ready:

1.  Open the project's **Proposal** tab.
2.  Select **Send Proposal to Customer**.
3.  If you have unsaved changes, select **Save & Send** instead.
4.  Choose how you want to share the proposal.

Available options can include:

*   **Email** — Send directly through OpenSolar. A customer contact with a valid email address is required.
*   **Share link** — Enable link sharing and copy the proposal URL.
*   **Direct sharing** — Send the copied link through your preferred communication method.

Customers can open the proposal on desktop, tablet, or mobile and move through the available chapters.

If checkout is enabled, they can also accept the proposal online.

## Limits and troubleshooting

| Situation | What to do |
| --- | --- |
| **You're working on a commercial project** | Swipe is not available. Use a **Scroll** proposal instead. |
| **Too many systems are selected** | Reduce the number of selected systems, including electrification systems, to **six or fewer** from the **Payments** tab. |
| **The Swipe card is unavailable or greyed out** | Check that the project is residential, has a valid design, and does not exceed the supported system limit. |
| **There is no Swipe template in Control** | Swipe may not be enabled for your organization. Contact OpenSolar Support. |
| **The preview says the project doesn't contain enough information** | Select a residential preview project with a completed design and payment options. |
| **The template card shows Updated** | The organization template has changed. Select **Override** to apply the latest version or **Cancel** to keep the project's current proposal. |
| **Checkout is disabled** | Enable checkout under **Advanced Settings**, or update the proposal's **Valid Until** date if checkout is configured to stop after expiry. |
| **The proposal looks different on mobile** | Use the device preview in **Full Screen** to check desktop, tablet, and mobile layouts before sending. |
